questions.question: What can gloves do for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Make it harder to control the motorcycle and should not be worn.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip on your motorcycle's handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: On which surface do motorcycle tires have the best grip?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces give poor traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all hazardous for motorcycles. Dry pavement is the safest.

questions.question: Which sign is usually rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other rule signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What best reduces the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may be going slowly while looking for spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars are dangerous for riders. A driver may pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: One front and one rear brake
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency

questions.correctAnswerText: One front and one rear brake
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your specific motorcycle?

options.text: Someone with a different type of motorcycle

questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before your first ride. This is important especially if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: When should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: Do not wear them because they make your hands too hot.
Wear them to get a better grip on the handlebars.
Do not wear them because they make controls harder to use.
Wear them only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear them to get a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or durable gloves when riding. They give you a better grip and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
It does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Helmets do not limit your vision. Any U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet allows you to see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need regular checking?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chain, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. A small mechanical problem can be very dangerous.

questions.question: Your body removes alcohol only through:
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, oil, and metal plates are all slippery. Dry pavement provides the best grip for tires.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: A high-quality helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road hazards and conditions.

questions.question: For best protection, boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be made of a soft material.
Have long laces that are not tucked in.
Cover the ankle and provide support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Keep heels low so they don't catch on things. Tuck in long laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: An adequate cushion of space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Allows you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Keeps you in a single area of the lane, limiting your movement.
Allows you to rely on others to identify hazards.
Requires you go faster to stay with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can more easily see the lights of other vehicles.
More difficult than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because visibility is poor. Without normal light and shadows, it is harder to judge distances.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can improve their visibility by:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors with reflective materials. Use your headlight at all times. Use your signals and brake light properly so others can see you.

questions.question: Maintain an adequate following distance behind other vehicles:

options.text: To allow you time and space to identify and react to hazards.
To allow for traffic counters to accurately count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To allow you time and space to identify and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you room to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, motorcycle riders should be especially cautious of:

options.text: Motorists looking for a place to park.

questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, watch for cars pulling away from the curb or backing out of parking spaces.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of for the best protection?
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another durable material to protect your hands.

questions.question: How often should you inspect your motorcycle before riding?
questions.explanation: Small mechanical problems can cause serious crashes on a motorcycle. Always inspect your motorcycle before every ride.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. What should you do to be more visible?
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen during the day, wear bright-colored clothing while riding to stay visible.

questions.question: What should you do with your feet when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep them firmly on the footrests
Keep them away from the controls

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them firmly on the footrests
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests for good balance. Do not drag them or point your toes down. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, at intersections, when changing lanes, and when turning.
